subject: Renewal & capacity uptick: proposal to migrate A100 → L40S and add reserved throughput
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Liam Chen <liam.chen@brightlinelabs.com>, procurement@brightlinelabs.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal & capacity uptick: proposal to migrate A100 → L40S and add reserved throughput

Hi Liam / BrightLine procurement team,

Thanks again for the productive QBR last week. Per our conversation, BrightLine’s current Dedicated pool (A100-heavy) will come up for renewal in July and you indicated interest in both growing reserved capacity and exploring a hardware class refresh to L40S to improve inference throughput per dollar.

Attached is a short proposal that sketches: (1) a 12‑month amendment with an 18% unit price uplift but a ~27% throughput improvement per reserved GPU when switching the same reserved count from A100→L40S, (2) a recommended reserved unit increase of +30% to cover peak batch windows, and (3) a proposed throughput SLA (99.5% for p95 latency at agreed seq lengths) with a small credit for missed SLOs.

High-level rationale: L40S shows lower inference cost on your production prompts due to higher sustained token throughput and better kernel utilization for mixed precision quantized weights. In practice we see customers reduce effective $/1000 tokens by ~15–30% when they regrade from A100 to L40S and align batching and prefix-caching. Ben and Marissa are looped to provide the benchmark details and the amendment draft.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben: share the workload-specific benchmark summary (attached) and a short performance-per-dollar note.
- Procurement: confirm the targeted reserved units for year 1 (baseline +30% suggested).
- I’ll follow up with a formal amendment and an SLA addendum for legal review.

Would you be open to a 30-minute call this week to walk the economics and the SLA language? We can also run a short warm-up benchmark on your production prompt set if you want the numbers validated on BrightLine traffic.

Thanks,

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0124

Attachments: Proposed_Amendment_BrightLine_v1.pdf (proposal), Throughput_Benchmark_SUMMARY.xlsx (benchmarks)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal & capacity uptick: proposal to migrate A100 → L40S and add reserved throughput

On Tue, Jun 15, 2027 at 09:12 AM Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Liam / BrightLine procurement team,
> ...

Quick internal note: I ran the BrightLine sample prompts (as requested) on our internal L40S and A100 configs with their mix of 1–4k token requests. Summary is attached (Throughput_Benchmark_SUMMARY.xlsx) — key points below: 

- Single-GPU sustained throughput: L40S > A100 by median 26% across the set (larger wins on batching-heavy prompts).
- Cost model (including reserved discount): when you amortize instance cost vs tokens served, L40S shows 18% mean reduction in $/1M tokens for BrightLine's profile.
- Operational caveat: L40S has different warm-up characteristics; recommend a short warm-up bucket (10–20 requests) and a small prefix cache to avoid cold bursts.

For the SLA ask: we can offer a p95 latency target with a throughput-floor guarantee (x tokens/sec per reserved GPU) tied to a usage profile. Need Marissa’s input on discounts/credit bands for missed SLOs.

I’ll prepare a 1‑page perf-per-dollar memo for the call and highlight recommended autoscaling/burst policy to limit over-provisioning.

Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachment: Throughput_Benchmark_SUMMARY.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 13:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal & capacity uptick: proposal to migrate A100 → L40S and add reserved throughput

Thanks Ben — great summary. Adding commercial notes: 

- Pricing: to make the economics simple for BrightLine, propose a 12‑month amendment that converts 60% of their current committed A100 units to L40S at a blended rate that nets them ~12% overall monthly spend neutrality in year 1 when combined with the recommended +30% reserved units. That creates headroom for throughput during peak jobs while still lowering $/token.
- Term & billing: 12 months with quarterly usage reviews (can trigger conversion to larger reserved tiers if they sustain higher throughput).
- SLA credit: 0.5% of monthly invoice per missed SLO tranche, capped at 3% — aligned with our typical Dedicated credit bands.
- Deal economics: recommend we keep an expansion incentive (1 month free on the incremental +30% capacity) to remove friction for procurement.

I’ll include these points in the amendment doc and circulate to legal. Olga — if procurement asks for a longer term (24 months) we can offer a slightly deeper blended discount (additional 5% off the blended unit price) in exchange for the longer commitment.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: Proposed_Amendment_BrightLine_v1.pdf
From: Liam Chen <liam.chen@brightlinelabs.com>

Cc: procurement@brightlinelabs.com, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal & capacity uptick: proposal to migrate A100 → L40S and add reserved throughput

Thanks Olga — appreciate the quick turnaround and the benchmark attachment. A few procurement items before we loop in legal: 

1) Can you provide a one-page performance-per-dollar summary that shows our current effective $/1M tokens on A100 vs the proposed blended L40S lineup (with the +30% reserved units)? We want to present a clear delta to execs.
2) We need the draft SLA addendum to show the latency p95 target and the exact crediting mechanism (same as you mentioned).
3) Are there any migration costs or one-time engineering support hours we should budget for? We want an apples-to-apples comparison.

Happy to do a 30-minute call on Monday (Jun 21) to review the documents and next steps. If you can include an explicit DocuSign-ready amendment and an estimate of migration support hours, procurement can fast-track this internally.

Best,
Liam Chen
Head of ML Platforms, BrightLine Labs
liam.chen@brightlinelabs.com
